1. Case 1: S. agalactiae mastitis
The postpartum woman presents with right breast erythema, pain, recurrent episodes, and bilateral milky discharge. Laboratory tests show leukocytosis and elevated CRP, and milk culture grew penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus agalactiae, confirming a bacterial infectious etiology. Ultrasound reveals no abscess or focal lesion, and physical exam shows no fluctuance, effectively excluding breast abscess and inflammatory breast cancer. Milk stasis remains a secondary contributor but is not the primary process. The evidence converges on high-confidence lactational mastitis caused by S. agalactiae, with confidence 0.9, and no further refinement is needed for clinical diagnosis.
